question: RNTCP stands for:
options: A. National Rural Tuberculosis Control Programme
B. Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme
C. Regional Nursing and Tuberculosis Care Programme
D. Rural National Health Tuberculosis Programme
explanation:
• RNTCP is Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (now under NTEP).
• DOTS is the strategy used.

question: IMR stands for:
explanation:
• IMR = deaths of infants under 1 year per 1000 live births.
• Key indicator of child health and health system performance.

question: Under UIP, BCG is given at:
explanation:
• BCG (for TB) is given at birth under Universal Immunization Programme.
• OPV-0 also at birth; DPT and others start at 6 weeks.

question: Level of prevention that includes immunization is:
explanation:
• Primary prevention prevents disease (immunization, health education).
• Secondary = early detection; Tertiary = rehabilitation.

question: NACP is related to:
explanation:
• NACP = National AIDS Control Programme.
• Focus on prevention, care, and treatment of HIV.

question: PHC stands for:
explanation:
• PHC is Primary Health Centre—first contact for community.
• Part of three-tier health system in India.

question: MMR in health statistics refers to:
explanation:
• MMR = Maternal Mortality Ratio (maternal deaths per 100,000 live births).
• Key indicator for maternal health programmes.

question: ORS is used mainly for:
explanation:
• Oral Rehydration Solution corrects fluid and electrolyte loss in diarrhea.
• WHO ORS formula is life-saving in childhood diarrhea.

question: RCH Programme focuses on:
explanation:
• RCH = Reproductive and Child Health (maternal, child, family planning).
• Now subsumed under NHM.

question: CBR in demography stands for:
explanation:
• CBR = Crude Birth Rate (live births per 1000 population per year).
• CDR = Crude Death Rate.

question: DOTS in TB control stands for:
explanation:
• DOTS = Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course. Ensures adherence to TB treatment.
• Key component of RNTCP/NTEP.

question: Epidemiology: incidence means:
options: A. Total cases at a point in time
B. New cases in a population over a period
explanation:
• Incidence = new cases in a period. Prevalence = total cases at a point in time.
• Both are measures of disease burden.

question: Primary Health Centre (PHC) typically covers population of:
explanation:
• PHC covers ~20,000-30,000 in plains; 20,000 in tribal/hilly areas.
• Sub-centre covers ~5000; CHC covers 80,000-120,000.

question: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) includes:
options: B. Malaria, dengue, filariasis, JE, kala-azar
explanation:
• NVBDCP: malaria, dengue, lymphatic filariasis, Japanese encephalitis, kala-azar.
• Vector control and prevention.

question: Health education method that is one-to-one is:
explanation:
• Individual: counseling, door-to-door. Group: discussion, demonstration. Mass: TV, radio, poster.
• Choose method per objective and audience.

question: Family planning method that is permanent for females:
explanation:
• Tubal ligation (female sterilization) is permanent. Vasectomy for males.
• IUCD (Copper-T), OCP are reversible.

question: Surveillance in public health means:
options: B. Continuous systematic collection and analysis of health data
explanation:
• Surveillance: ongoing collection, analysis, interpretation of data for action.
• Used for outbreak detection and programme planning.

question: CDR stands for:
explanation:
• CDR = Crude Death Rate (deaths per 1000 population per year).
• With CBR gives natural growth rate.

question: Under NHM, ASHA stands for:
explanation:
• ASHA = Accredited Social Health Activist. Link between community and health system.
• Key under National Health Mission.

question: Secondary prevention includes:
explanation:
• Secondary: screening, early diagnosis, treatment to prevent progression.
• e.g. Pap smear, blood sugar screening.

question: Epidemic means:
options: B. Occurrence of disease in excess of expected in a community
explanation:
• Epidemic: excess of cases in area. Pandemic: worldwide. Endemic: constant presence.
• Outbreak often used for limited epidemic.

question: ORS composition includes:
explanation:
• WHO ORS: sodium, potassium, glucose, bicarbonate (or citrate). Promotes absorption.
• Correct preparation critical.

question: Tertiary prevention includes:
explanation:
• Tertiary: rehabilitation, disability limitation, prevent complications.
• e.g. cardiac rehab, diabetic foot care.

question: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is under:
options: A. RCH/NHM - conditional cash transfer for institutional delivery
explanation:
• JSY: cash incentive for institutional delivery to reduce MMR.
• Part of RCH/NHM.

question: Prevalence in epidemiology is:
options: B. Total cases (old + new) at a point in time
explanation:
• Prevalence = all cases at a point/period. Point vs period prevalence.
• Prevalence ≈ Incidence × Duration.

question: Sub-centre covers population of about:
explanation:
• Sub-centre: 3000-5000 (5000 in tribal/hilly). First contact.
• Staff: ANM, multipurpose worker.

question: Pulse Polio programme aims to:
explanation:
• Pulse Polio: supplementary immunization to eradicate polio.
• India declared polio-free in 2014.

question: Source of infection in epidemiology can be:
explanation:
• Reservoir/source: human, animal, or environment where pathogen lives.
• Understanding source helps control.

question: NHM stands for:
explanation:
• NHM = National Health Mission (rural + urban). Includes NRHM, NUHM.
• ASHA, JSY, RCH, immunization under NHM.

question: IMNCI stands for:
options: A. Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness
B. Infant Mortality National Care Initiative
C. Immunization and Nutrition Child Initiative
explanation:
• IMNCI: integrated approach to manage sick children (feeding, danger signs, referral).
• Reduces child mortality.

question: Epidemiological triad includes:
explanation:
• Triad: agent (pathogen), host (human/animal), environment.
• Change in any can alter disease occurrence.

question: MMR vaccine under UIP is given at:
explanation:
• MR/MMR: first dose 9-12 months, second 16-24 months (under UIP).
• Measles, mumps, rubella.

question: Census in India is conducted every:
explanation:
• Census every 10 years. Provides demographic and health-related data.
• Last census 2011; 2021 postponed.

question: Disease eradication means:
options: B. Zero incidence globally with no need for continued measures
explanation:
• Eradication: permanent reduction to zero (e.g. smallpox). Elimination: zero in region.
• Polio nearly eradicated.

question: Antenatal care (ANC) aims to:
options: B. Detect risk, promote health, prepare for delivery
explanation:
• ANC: risk detection, health promotion, birth preparedness, complication readiness.
• At least 4 ANC visits recommended.
